issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer replays records via LoggingHandler.emit which re-runs filters and may double-log
issues.detail: Replaying buffered records through the OTLP LoggingHandler's emit() will re-evaluate filters (including the JobContext log filter) and propagate to anything attached. If any of the buffered records were already emitted via another path or have stale context, you risk duplicate exports or incorrect contextual tagging. Consider directly invoking the underlying log_emitter rather than re-emitting.

issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry removes ALL LoggingHandlers from root, including non-OTLP ones with same class name
issues.detail: The loop removes every LoggingHandler instance, but if a user has independently attached an opentelemetry LoggingHandler to a different LoggerProvider (e.g. their own telemetry stack), it will be silently torn down. Scope removal to handlers tied to the specific logger_provider being shut down.

issues.description: _BufferingHandler.buffer is unbounded; long pre-connect crashes can OOM the process
issues.detail: Buffering begins at _run_job_task start with no size cap. If a job hangs before session.start() while emitting heavy logs (retries, network spam, debug logging), the list grows without bound. Add a maxlen (deque) or byte cap and drop-oldest with a warning record.

issues.description: init_recording in _on_cleanup may run telemetry setup on a closing event loop
issues.detail: _on_cleanup is called during shutdown; init_recording calls _setup_cloud_tracer which typically creates OTLP exporters/threads and async resources. Setting these up at cleanup time and then immediately calling _shutdown_telemetry risks losing the flushed logs or hitting a closed loop. Verify _setup_cloud_tracer is safe at cleanup and that force_flush actually drains before shutdown.

issues.description: Removing pytest-xdist (-n auto) and dropping test_plugin_google_stt.py from CI is unexplained
issues.detail: The makefile change serializes unit tests and silently drops a test file. This will slow CI substantially and removes coverage with no rationale in the PR description. If the google_stt test is flaky, that should be tracked; if -n auto is causing issues, it should be diagnosed rather than disabled wholesale.

issues.description: _on_entry_done forces shutdown_fut even when job already called shutdown, masking original reason
issues.detail: The InvalidStateError suppression handles the race, but when an exception occurs after a legitimate shutdown was initiated, the 'job crashed' reason now overwrites nothing (set_result fails) — fine. However, if a task exception occurs concurrently with normal completion, the ordering of reasons is non-obvious. A short comment clarifying intent would help future maintainers.

review.summary: The PR's core fix — buffering early logs and flushing them on crash — is well-motivated, but the implementation has a few sharp edges: unbounded buffer, broad LoggingHandler removal during shutdown, replay through the handler pipeline rather than the emitter, and late telemetry init during cleanup. Separately, the makefile change quietly disables xdist and removes a test file with no rationale. Consider tightening handler scoping, bounding the buffer, and clarifying the test-runner changes before merge.
